correctness.rationale: At stationarity the independent Poisson reset age is E/r with E unit exponential. Integration of the zero-state velocity equation and Brownian scaling give the claimed coupling with h(w)=Mr(1−e^(−w/(Mr))) and diffusing orientation U_r(z)=(cos(√(2/r)W_z),sin(√(2/r)W_z)). Independently split the active error into coefficient, orientation and kernel defects. The coefficient defect is bounded by |α_r−α| times the L² norm of E²/2, namely √6. Conditional on E=s, the orientation L² defect is at most α√(2/r)∫₀ˢ(s−z)√z dz=4α√(2/r)s^(5/2)/15; averaging gives 16√15 α/(15√r). Using 0≤w−h(w)≤w²/(2Mr) bounds the active kernel defect by αE³/(6Mr), of norm 2√5 α/(Mr). The two-dimensional thermal Itô isometry gives squared kernel error at most E[E⁵]/(5M²r²)=24/(M²r²). Their sum bounds W₂ for all r>0. Conditioning on the age gives mean αs²e₁/2 and covariance 2s³I₂/3; direct Gaussian mixing gives the stated characteristic function and density (possible divergence at the reset point). With A=E²/2, D=A−1 and v=2E³/3, the factorial identities give E[D³]=74 and E[Dv]=36; conditional centering then gives both third moments and the displayed covariance. Bounds by exponential-age moments give uniform integrability at every fixed order and Lᵖ convergence on the same coupling. For diverging α_r, division by α_r removes the thermal term and gives the strictly positive-magnitude age-square limit, so the original scale escapes in probability. This is a stationary one-time position law for complete resets to a fixed heading, not an assumption of constant orientation between resets or a statement on position-only resetting. The supplied finite checker was read, not run.

value.rationale: The result distinguishes three physically meaningful scales and gives a quantitative law for the regime where propulsion and thermal fluctuations have comparable size. A scalar second moment does not tell whether the position is Gaussian or whether the orthogonal fluctuation size depends on the longitudinal displacement. The common-age mixture, asymmetric moments and explicit rate supply that information and a finite-rate accuracy benchmark under the specified reset protocol.
